 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The New York Giants are looking to bounce back against the Jacksonville Jaguars this Sunday after a 24-21 loss to Washington. Head coach John Harbaugh expected routine questions from reporters on Friday about that game, but one stunned him with breaking news that upended his staff's scouting plans for next week.
 The Indianapolis Colts had just released former Giants quarterback Daniel Jones . Their sudden midseason move left Harbaugh briefly speechless at the podium.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement John Harbaugh freezes at podium as Colts cut Daniel Jones 
 A reporter asked Harbaugh if the sudden quarterback change disrupts the scouts already studying Indianapolis film for next week's matchup. Harbaugh froze in that second with wide eyes and a blank stare as he processed the news.
 Sep 27, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh calls a time out during the fourth quarter against the Tennessee Titans at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images
 "Yeah, probably pretty dramatically. Wow, I don't want to get ahead of ourselves here, and you just hit me with that," he replied .
 Indianapolis fell to 3-8 after a blowout 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans on Thursday night. Jones completed just 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards while throwing an interception in his sixth straight game. That turnover streak capped a rough 11-game stint in which he passed for 1,974 yards and threw 13 interceptions against just seven touchdowns.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Colts coach Shane Steichen actually benched Jones midway through the fourth quarter against Houston and sent in Anthony Richardson Sr., who is going to start for Indianapolis from now on.
 Just days earlier, the Colts coach had defended Jones after a 24-22 win over Miami despite two interceptions and insisted his own play-calling needed to improve. Steichen reversed course on Friday and announced the release was in the best interests of both sides.
 Giants prep for Anthony Richardson as Colts absorb steep contract hit 
 Richardson Sr. will make his first start in two years against Harbaugh's defense on Nov. 29. Since the 2023 fourth overall pick plays a completely different style than Jones, New York's scouts must scrap most of their old notes and start fresh on film.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Harbaugh added, "Definitely the offense will be the offense that they run, but it'll be centered around the quarterback for sure. And they're probably different styles to some degree. We'll have to look at that when the time comes and our people, we have people doing that this week, they'll have to make a left turn obviously."
 Indianapolis absorbed a massive financial hit to cut ties rather than keep Jones as a backup. He signed a two-year $88 million extension in March with $50 million guaranteed and a $10.51 million injury guarantee for next season.
 By releasing him healthy, the Colts avoided owing that extra money next year even though Spotrac shows they still carry $14.9 million in dead cap this season and $35.2 million in 2027.
 While Indianapolis resets at quarterback, Harbaugh has found stability in New York with J.J. McCarthy. The former Vikings signal-caller has gone 2-1 as a starter with 915 yards and a 63.5 percent completion rate to keep the Giants atop the NFC East.
